title: Turkey Tetrazzini
subtitle: A baked pasta casserole using leftover turkey
excerpt: The classic American post-holiday casserole. Pulled turkey and mushrooms in a sherry cream sauce, baked with spaghetti and a Parmesan crumb on top.
sourceNotes: American Thanksgiving and Christmas leftover dish. Follows the same structure as Chicken Tetrazzini but uses turkey crown or leftover roast turkey.

recipe.freezeNotes: Assemble and freeze before baking. Thaw overnight in the fridge. Bake from cold, adding 15 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Works well in two dishes for a crowd. The sauce doubles easily.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to a day ahead. Refrigerate covered. Bake to order.

content.text: This is the dish that earns its place the day after a big roast. The turkey is already cooked, so the work is the sauce. Keep the sauce loose before baking; it will thicken in the oven.
Heat the oven to 190C. Cook the spaghetti in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Drain and set aside.
Melt 20g butter in the frying pan over high heat. Cook the mushrooms for 5 minutes until golden. Season and set aside.
Melt the remaining butter in the large saucepan over medium heat. Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the sherry and stir until absorbed. Pour in the milk and stock gradually, stirring constantly, until the sauce is smooth and thick.
Stir in the cream, nutmeg, half the Parmesan, salt, and pepper. Remove from the heat.
Toss the spaghetti, turkey, mushrooms, peas if using, and sauce together in the roasting tin until well combined.
Mix the remaining Parmesan with the breadcrumbs. Scatter over the top. Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest for 5 minutes.

items.symptom: The pasta is clumped and dry.
items.cause: The sauce was too thick before baking or the pasta was fully cooked.
items.fix: Stop pasta 2 minutes early. Thin the sauce with a splash of stock before assembling.

items.symptom: The dish smells strongly of sherry.
items.cause: The sherry was not cooked off in the sauce.
items.fix: Let the sherry bubble for 2 full minutes after adding it to the roux.

items.symptom: The crumb topping sinks into the sauce.
items.cause: The sauce was too wet when assembled.
items.fix: Let the sauce reduce for an extra 2 minutes before combining.
